inputs: Exactly five complete unsegmented support demonstrations. Each is a list of (pre-action observable four bits, native action) ending at the recorded terminal observation with the STOP label. At decision time supply only the current four Boolean predicates plus the policy's own past observed predicates and executed commands. A complete support trajectory is authorized; a held-out trajectory, endpoint, source program, donor rank, task ID and semantic phase are unavailable. No method gets a move annotation or uses a first-move rule.
api: remote/karel_unaligned_baselines.py build(method, support); returned policy.act(obs) is non-mutating, policy.advance(obs, action) records an executed action. Methods suffix_live, suffix_initial, suffix_masked, modal_plan, index_vote, dtw_uniform, dtw_actions_only, dtw_support_weighted. STOP is an ordinary decision during action selection. Repeated act calls at the same boundary must not advance the policy.
suffix: Import the original suffix vote, history limit, observation feature sets, action-only fallback, and STOP-then-lexical tie break unchanged from remote/karel_online_control.py. These are the original flat comparators applied to the same observation channel.
clock_controls: modal_plan chooses the modal complete support command sequence once, tie resolved by lexical ordering of the primitive tuples (shorter exact prefix first). It follows the chosen plan, returning STOP beyond its end. index_vote is a separate clock-only control: use the current number of previously executed non-STOP commands as a generic index in each support, treating every completed donor as STOP, and vote. Action-vote ties prefer STOP, then lexical native name.
alignment: The three dtw_* method keys use a monotone donor-prefix edit-distance alignment with gaps, not symmetric offline DTW. For each donor, maintain distance D(t,j) of the already executed t query events to its first j executed primitive events. D(0,j)=16j and D(t,0)=16t. Update by the minimum of diagonal plus 16 for a nonmatching command plus weighted Hamming distance of pre-action observations, deleting a donor event at cost 16, or inserting the query event at cost 16. At a decision boundary, every donor prefix j=0..L, including its STOP boundary, competes at cost D(t,j) plus weighted Hamming distance from the current query observation to the donor's next pre-action observation. Find the global minimum; among minimizing donors each donor casts one vote split equally over its distinct minimizing next labels. An exactly tied label vote prefers STOP then lexical native action name. Never retrospectively align to future query observations. All donor positions are allowed and receive only the generic accumulated gap cost, with no semantic anchor. No execution pins a single donor or assumes it is correct.

weights.dtw_uniform: Untrained fixed weights (4,4,4,4), aggregate maximum 16 equals one full action mismatch or gap.
weights.dtw_actions_only: Identical recurrence, detector and voting, but all four sensor weights are fixed at zero.
weights.dtw_support_weighted: The search, gap and action costs and tie rules match dtw_uniform exactly. For each of the ten unordered pairs of training demonstrations compare positions with the same generic command index and equal immediately preceding primitive (or common start). Include terminal positions at their actual index, with no fabricated padding. For each sensor bit estimate p(next labels disagree | bit differs) and p(next labels disagree | bit matches) using add-one-smoothed Bernoulli frequencies within these matched examples. If at least one count group is empty, set that bit weight to zero. Otherwise use max(0, the difference). Multiply by 16 and round to the nearest integer (half up). Each weight thus lies in [0,16]. No tuning, cross-program aggregation, target data or marker-specific treatment. This support-only salience baseline can overfit correlated bits and may fail when aligned contexts are scarce.

fairness: Same five supports and observation/action budget for all policies. Enforce common environment and rollout limit externally, and distinguish full free rollout from single teacher-forced prediction. A policy can succeed by generic time-index alone on synchronized demonstrations. It can also exploit a pre-action sensor correlated with the start world; comparisons among sensor-masked/initial-only and uniform aligner distinguish some of these effects. A matched recurrent representation with randomized/untrained weights remains the appropriate like-for-like control for a separate learned representation. This implementation runs no school jobs itself.
